# 🐶 BillDog MCP Server **Set up and inspect [BillDog](https://billdog.io) paywalls, subscriptions and analytics for your app — from your AI coding agent.** [![MCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP-Streamable%20HTTP-6E56CF)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) [![Tools](https://img.shields.io/badge/tools-55-2ea44f)](#tools) [![Auth](https://img.shields.io/badge/auth-OAuth%202.1%20%2B%20PKCE-0969da)](#sign-in-with-billdog) [![Docs](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-billdog.io-black)](https://billdog.io/docs/mcp-server) `https://api.billdog.io/mcp` [Install](#install) · [What you can ask](#what-you-can-ask) · [Tools](#tools) · [Permissions](#permissions--safety) · [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)
--- [BillDog](https://billdog.io) is paywalls, in-app purchases, subscriptions, analytics, messaging, surveys and journeys behind one SDK for iOS, Android, React Native, Flutter, Expo and the web. This repository is how AI agents connect to it: - **A hosted MCP server.** 60 tools: diagnose an integration, record the app's bundle ID and package name, build the product catalog, design and publish paywalls, and query revenue and retention. - **Plugins for Claude Code, Cursor and Antigravity.** The server plus five skills: wiring the SDK into an app, custom (headless) paywall UI, paywall A/B experiments and feature flags, revenue and conversion analysis, and migrating from RevenueCat, Superwall, Adapty and others. Nothing runs on your machine. The server is hosted by BillDog and every client connects to the same URL. ## Install You need a free BillDog account at [billdog.io](https://billdog.io) with at least one project. | Client | How | |---|---| | **Claude Code** (plugin, recommended) | `/plugin marketplace add billdogai/billdog-mcp`, then `/plugin install billdog@billdog` | | **Claude Code** (server only) | `claude mcp add --transport http billdog https://api.billdog.io/mcp` | | **Claude.ai / Claude Desktop** | Settings → Connectors → **Add custom connector** → paste `https://api.billdog.io/mcp` | | **Cursor** | Settings → MCP → Add server, or the config below | | **VS Code (Copilot)** | Command palette → *MCP: Add Server* → HTTP → paste the URL | | **Antigravity** | Add the server to `mcp_config.json` using the config below | | **Windsurf / others** | Any client that supports remote Streamable HTTP servers | The first time a tool runs, your browser opens **Sign in with BillDog**. That's the whole setup.
Config file snippets **Cursor** (`~/.cursor/mcp.json`) and most clients: ```json { "mcpServers": { "billdog": { "url": "https://api.billdog.io/mcp" } } } ``` **VS Code** (`.vscode/mcp.json`): ```json { "servers": { "billdog": { "type": "http", "url": "https://api.billdog.io/mcp" } } } ``` **Antigravity** (`mcp_config.json`, which uses `serverUrl` rather than `url`): ```json { "mcpServers": { "billdog": { "serverUrl": "https://api.billdog.io/mcp" } } } ``` **Clients that only launch local (stdio) servers**, bridged with [`mcp-remote`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/mcp-remote): ```json { "mcpServers": { "billdog": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", "https://api.billdog.io/mcp"] } } } ```
## Sign in with BillDog The server uses OAuth 2.1 with PKCE and dynamic client registration, so your client registers and authenticates itself: 1. Your client discovers the authorization server from the server's `401` ([RFC 9728](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9728)). 2. It registers itself and opens BillDog in your browser. 3. You sign in, pick **one project**, and choose what the agent may do. 4. The agent gets a short-lived token for that project only. It refreshes on its own, and you can disconnect it at any time. ### Using a key instead For scripts, CI, or clients without OAuth, create a key at **[Dashboard → AI Assistant (MCP) Keys](https://billdog.io/dashboard/analytics/api-keys)**. MCP keys start with `bd_mcp_` and are **read-only**. ```bash claude mcp add --transport http billdog https://api.billdog.io/mcp \ --header "Authorization: Bearer bd_mcp_YOUR_KEY" ``` > [!IMPORTANT] > `bd_public_…` and `bd_secret_…` keys are **SDK keys** for your app and won't work here. The server tells you so if you paste one. ## What you can ask > *"Why isn't my paywall showing on iOS?"* > → `get_setup_status` and `resolve_placement_preview` show exactly what's missing, with dashboard links. > *"Set up monthly and annual Pro plans with a 7-day trial and an `onboarding` placement."* > → `apply_setup_plan` creates the products, entitlement, offering and placement in one step. Everything starts inactive. > *"Design a dark paywall for the annual plan from a template, show me a preview, then publish it."* > → `list_templates` → `create_paywall_from_template` → `update_paywall` → `preview_paywall` → `publish_paywall` > *"What was MRR last month and which paywall converts best?"* > → `run_analytics_query` > *"Migrate this app from RevenueCat."* > → the `billdog-migration` skill (Claude Code plugin) rewrites the call sites and recreates the catalog. ## Tools **29 read** · **31 write** · *publish* means it changes what live users see and needs the publish permission. On a live project (or one set to always require approval), those changes and any change to an entitlement's products are not applied: the tool returns an `approve_url`, the project's owners and admins are emailed, and an owner or admin approves it in the dashboard. Machine-readable list: [`tools.json`](tools.json). ### Setup & diagnostics | Tool | Access | What it does | |---|---|---| | `get_setup_status` | read | Inspect the setup status of BillDog for this project. | | `get_project` | read | Get project metadata including bundle ID, package name, and registered domains. | | `get_recent_sdk_activity` | read | Is the app sending data? For the last window_hours (default 24): events by name, purchases and session replays, split into sandbox and production, with has_traffic for each. | | `resolve_placement_preview` | read | Dry-run preview of what a client SDK receives when resolving a placement. | | `get_sdk_integration_guide` | read | Get the code to add BillDog to an app on one platform: iOS, Android, React Native, Flutter, Expo or web. | ### Analytics | Tool | Access | What it does | |---|---|---| | `run_analytics_query` | read | Run a single analytics report. | | `discover_schema` | read | Return the full BillDog analytics schema — every (source, metric) pairing the project supports, with a 1-line description of what each returns. | | `list_event_names` | read | List the event names this project received in the last `days` days (default 30), most frequent first, with each one's count and unique users. | | `list_cohorts` | read | List saved cohorts for this project. | | `list_saved_views` | read | List saved analytics views for this project, each with what it asks (source, metric, dims, filters, date range, segment). | | `get_saved_view_results` | read | Re-run a saved view and return its results. | ### Catalog: products, entitlements, offerings, placements | Tool | Access | What it does | |---|---|---| | `list_products` | read | List all products configured in this project's catalog, including their identifiers, product types, subscription durations, and store mapping IDs. | | `list_entitlements` | read | List all entitlements in this project and the product IDs associated with each entitlement. | | `list_offerings` | read | List all offerings in this project, showing their packages, attached products, and default/current status. | | `list_placements` | read | List all placements in this project, including access gating settings and linked offerings. | | `apply_setup_plan` | write · publish | Declaratively evaluate and execute a complete monetization catalog setup (products, entitlements, offerings, packages, placements). | | `create_product` | write | Create a store product (subscription or in-app purchase) in the project catalog. | | `update_product` | write | Update metadata, store IDs, or display pricing for an existing product in this project. | | `create_entitlement` | write | Create a new entitlement in the catalog and optionally link it to products. | | `update_entitlement` | write | Update display name, description, or linked products for an existing entitlement (product_ids replaces the list). On a live project a change to its products waits for approval. | | `set_entitlement_products` | write | Set the explicit list of product IDs granting an entitlement (replaces the list; only the links that change are touched). On a live project it waits for approval. | | `create_offering` | write | Create a new offering with packages. | | `manage_offering_packages` | write | Add or remove packages within an existing offering. | | `set_current_offering` | write · publish | Make an offering the project current offering (the others stop being current, atomically). | | `create_placement` | write | Create a new placement in the project. | | `link_placement` | write · publish | Link one or more offerings to a placement with priority order (replaces its links). | ### Paywalls | Tool | Access | What it does | |---|---|---| | `list_paywalls` | read | List all paywalls in this project, including active state, wall type, and publication timestamps. | | `get_paywall` | read | Get a paywall by UUID or identifier: status, layouts, offering, colours and copy_outline — every text and button with its component id, for update_paywall patch.copy. include_config returns the full draft and published configs (large). | | `list_templates` | read | List available paywall and onboarding templates from the BillDog template catalog. | | `create_paywall_from_template` | write | Create a new paywall in the project from an existing template. | | `design_paywall` | write | Design a paywall and save it as an inactive draft. | | `update_paywall` | write | Apply constrained patch updates to a paywall's draft (copy, title, subtitle, CTA text, brand colors, offering binding). | | `preview_paywall` | read | Evaluate paywall publish gate (validating components, bindings, offerings) and generate a secure short-lived preview link and token. | | `publish_paywall` | write · publish | Publish a draft paywall to make it active for SDK delivery. | | `unpublish_paywall` | write · publish | Deactivate an active paywall. | | `get_paywall_recipe_guide` | read | Get the full guide to writing a design_paywall `recipe`: every node type and its fields, theme tokens, icons, dynamic price values, layout and design advice. | ### Experiments & feature flags | Tool | Access | What it does | |---|---|---| | `list_experiments` | read | List the project's experiments with their status, what devices are served now (variants, the shipped winner, or the control only), and each variant's paywall and traffic share. | | `create_experiment` | write | Create a paywall A/B experiment as a DRAFT: each variant shows a different paywall at the same place in the app. | | `start_experiment` | write · publish | Start (or resume) an experiment: users who reach its paywall are split between the variants. | | `stop_experiment` | write · publish | Stop an experiment: pause or end it (everyone sees the control paywall), or end it and ship the winning variant to everyone. | | `get_experiment_results` | read | Per-variant results of an experiment for its whole run: users, conversions, conversion rate, revenue per user, lift vs control, p-value and significance (p < 0.05 with 100+ users per arm), plus a verdict: winner, loser, keep_running or no_data. | | `list_feature_flags` | read | List the project's feature flags: key, on/off, rollout percentage, variants, and whether it has release conditions (audience rules, edited in the dashboard). | | `create_feature_flag` | write | Create a feature flag, OFF: every user gets false until update_feature_flag turns it on. | | `update_feature_flag` | write · publish | Turn a feature flag on (start) or off (stop), change its rollout percentage or variants, or rename it. | | `get_feature_flag_results` | read | How many users and evaluations got each value of a flag over the last N days (default 30, max 90), from the $feature_flag_called events the SDKs send. | ### Projects & SDK keys | Tool | Access | What it does | |---|---|---| | `list_projects` | read | List all BillDog projects accessible to the authenticated user, identifying the current active project, bundle ID, and platform. | | `create_project` | write | Create a new BillDog project for the authenticated user with a specified name, bundle ID, and platform. | | `create_public_sdk_key` | write | Generate a client-safe public SDK key (bd_public_live_... or bd_public_test_...) for mobile and web apps. | | `add_app` | write | Record the app's iOS bundle ID, Android package name or web domain, one per platform, exactly as the user gives it. An app already recorded is changed on the dashboard's Apps tab; not available on a live project. | | `use_project` | write | Switch this connection to another project it may use: the project chosen when it was connected, or one it created with create_project. | ### Engagement: surveys, campaigns, journeys, messages | Tool | Access | What it does | |---|---|---| | `list_surveys` | read | List all multi-page surveys and micro-survey walls configured for this project. | | `create_survey` | write | Save a survey as a DRAFT with its questions (activate it in the dashboard). | | `list_campaigns` | read | List all marketing and engagement campaigns configured for this project. | | `create_campaign` | write | Save a campaign as a DRAFT. | | `list_journeys` | read | List all customer onboarding and engagement journeys with their sequence of steps. | | `create_journey` | write | Save a linear journey as a DRAFT (activate it with activate_journey or in the dashboard; branches are built on its canvas). | | `activate_journey` | write · publish | Activate a draft or paused journey so new matching events enroll customers. On a live project it files an approval request for an owner or admin instead. | | `pause_journey` | write · publish | Pause an active journey: nobody new enters, and people already in it are held where they are. On a live project it files an approval request instead. | | `list_message_templates` | read | List the project's message templates (push, in-app, email, SMS) with their title and body, as the dashboard Templates library shows them. | | `create_message_template` | write | Save a reusable push or in-app message template (the same kind the dashboard Templates library shows). | ## Permissions & safety | Guarantee | How | |---|---| | **One project per connection** | The project is fixed by your sign-in or key. Project ids in tool arguments are ignored, so the agent can't read another project. | | **You choose the access** | On the consent screen: read only, read + create/edit, or read + create/edit + publish. Keys are always read-only. | | **Nothing goes live by accident** | New products, offerings, placements and paywalls start inactive or as drafts. Publishing, starting experiments, activating journeys, setting the current offering and linking a placement with live traffic need the publish permission. | | **No customer contact data** | Email, phone, display name and custom attributes are withheld from every response, and the response says so. | | **Audited** | Every write is recorded in the project's audit log, attributed to the agent and the user who connected it. | | **Revocable** | Disconnect an agent, or revoke a key, from the dashboard at any time. | ## Claude Code plugin `/plugin install billdog@billdog` gives you the server plus five skills: - **`billdog-integration`**: adds the SDK to an app (Web, React Native, Expo, iOS, Android) or diagnoses one that's already wired. It covers the identifier traps (`@billdog.io`, not `@billdog`; `io.billdog`, not `com.billdog`), configuration, placements and a verification checklist. - **`billdog-migration`**: moves an app off RevenueCat, Superwall, Adapty, Mixpanel, Amplitude, OneSignal, Braze, Typeform or SurveyMonkey. It covers both the code and the data. - **`billdog-experiments`**: runs paywall A/B experiments and feature flags: create, start, read results, ship the winner, roll a flag out. - **`billdog-headless`**: builds a custom paywall screen in the app's own UI (SwiftUI, Compose, React Native, Expo, Flutter, web) or a game engine over REST: fetch the placement's offering, handle holdout, withheld and gated results, buy, and track impressions. - **`billdog-analyst`**: answers questions about the project's numbers (revenue, MRR, churn, renewals, trial conversion, LTV, paywall and placement conversion, funnels), picking the right report and reading it without the usual traps. Read-only. ## Cursor plugin The Cursor manifest is `.cursor-plugin/plugin.json`: the server, the five skills above and an always-on rule (`.cursor-plugin/rules/billdog.mdc`). To try a local checkout, copy or link the repository into `~/.cursor/plugins/local/billdog` and run *Developer: Reload Window*. ## Gemini CLI extension ```bash gemini extensions install https://github.com/billdogai/billdog-mcp ``` `gemini-extension.json` adds the server over Streamable HTTP; the first BillDog tool call opens Sign in with BillDog. The five skills in `skills/` load with it. ## Antigravity plugin ```bash agy plugin install https://github.com/billdogai/billdog-mcp ``` Installs the server, the five skills above and an always-on rule (`rules/AGENTS.md`) that has the agent read your live project before writing identifiers into code and ask before anything goes live. The first BillDog tool call opens Sign in with BillDog. To try a local checkout, run `agy plugin validate --strict .` and `agy plugin install .` from the repository root. ## Troubleshooting | Message | Fix | |---|---| | *"This is a BillDog SDK key…"* | You pasted a `bd_public_`/`bd_secret_` key. Use Sign in with BillDog, or create a `bd_mcp_` key. | | *"This key has MCP access turned off"* | Turn MCP access on for the key on the [MCP keys page](https://billdog.io/dashboard/analytics/api-keys). | | *…lacks the `mcp:write` scope* | Keys are read-only. Connect with Sign in with BillDog and allow **Create and edit configuration** (or **Publish and go live** for `mcp:publish`). | | Browser didn't open | Run `/mcp` in Claude Code and choose **Authenticate**, or reconnect the connector. | | *"Unknown or revoked client_id"* | Remove the BillDog server from your client and add it again. | ## Repository layout One plugin at the repository root, in two formats so every client can read it: ``` .cursor-plugin/plugin.json Cursor plugin manifest (Cursor Marketplace) gemini-extension.json Gemini CLI extension manifest .cursor-plugin/rules/billdog.mdc Cursor always-on rule plugin.json Agent Plugins 1.0.0 manifest (cursor.directory, other clients) mcp.json Agent Plugins 1.0.0 MCP config (streamable-http) skills/ billdog-integration, billdog-migration, billdog-experiments, billdog-analyst, billdog-headless (shared by every format) .claude-plugin/marketplace.json Claude Code marketplace (this repo) .claude-plugin/plugin.json Claude Code plugin manifest .mcp.json Claude Code MCP config server.json official MCP Registry entry smithery.yaml Smithery (stdio bridge via mcp-remote) glama.json Glama ownership claim tools.json all 60 tools, grouped, with access level .antigravity-plugin/plugin.json Antigravity plugin manifest (takes precedence over plugin.json in Antigravity) mcp_config.json Antigravity MCP config rules/AGENTS.md Antigravity always-on rule assets/icon.png listing icon assets/logo.png Antigravity logo (transparent background) ``` ## Use BillDog in your app The MCP server configures BillDog; your app talks to it through an SDK. | Platform | Package | Docs | |---|---|---| | iOS (Swift) | [billdog-ios-spm](https://github.com/billdogai/billdog-ios-spm) | [iOS guide](https://billdog.io/docs/ios) | | Android (Kotlin) | [billdog-android-full](https://github.com/billdogai/billdog-android-full) · [billdog-android-eng](https://github.com/billdogai/billdog-android-eng) | [Android guide](https://billdog.io/docs/android) | | React Native · Flutter · Web | npm · pub.dev | [React Native](https://billdog.io/docs/react-native) · [Flutter](https://billdog.io/docs/flutter) · [Web](https://billdog.io/docs/web) | | Superwall bridge (iOS) | [billdog-ios-superwall](https://github.com/billdogai/billdog-ios-superwall) | [Superwall integration](https://billdog.io/docs/superwall-integration) | | Server (Go, PHP, Node, Python…) | [billdogeng-go](https://github.com/billdogai/billdogeng-go) · [billdogeng-php](https://github.com/billdogai/billdogeng-php) | [Server SDKs](https://billdog.io/docs/server-sdk) | Not sure which one you need? See [choosing an SDK](https://billdog.io/docs/sdk-selection). ## Links - 🌐 Website: [billdog.io](https://billdog.io) — paywalls, subscriptions, analytics and experiments for mobile and web apps - 📖 Docs: [billdog.io/docs/mcp-server](https://billdog.io/docs/mcp-server) - 🧱 Paywall builder: [billdog.io/docs/paywall-builder](https://billdog.io/docs/paywall-builder) - 🧪 A/B experiments: [billdog.io/docs/experiments](https://billdog.io/docs/experiments) - 📊 Product analytics: [billdog.io/docs/product-analytics](https://billdog.io/docs/product-analytics) - 🧭 Full SDK reference for agents: [billdog.io/SKILL.md](https://billdog.io/SKILL.md) - 🐛 Issues: [github.com/billdogai/billdog-mcp/issues](https://github.com/billdogai/billdog-mcp/issues)
